modules.name: Qorvo DWM3001C UWB module
modules.summary: Fully integrated ultra-wideband (UWB) transceiver module for precise two-way ranging and RTLS positioning — the Qorvo DW3110 UWB IC + a Nordic nRF52833 BLE MCU + PCB antenna in one module.
notes: UWB ranging accuracy depends on ANTENNA POLARIZATION. The DWM3001C antenna is vertically polarized, so mount every module UPRIGHT and keep all anchors AND tags co-polarized (all vertical). If two antennas are perpendicular to each other the link uses the horizontally-polarized pattern, which has NULLS at some angles that cut range and add location error. This applies to essentially every UWB ranging device (anchor + tag), not just the DWM3001C. [Qorvo DWM3001C datasheet Rev F, Oct 2025, §6 Antenna Performance, Table 11]
AES key is stored in OTP (0x078-0x07F, big-endian) for secure ranging. [DWM3001C datasheet, memory map]

spec.source: Qorvo DWM3001C datasheet Rev F, Oct 2025

not_for: running application code (it is a debug probe, not a target)

modules.name: STLINK-V3MINIE (ST debug probe)
modules.summary: Compact standalone STM32/STM8 debug probe (SWD + virtual COM port) in a low-cost minimal form factor.
good_for: embedding a probe into a custom fixture
not_for: running application code (it is a debug probe, not a target)

modules.name: ST-LINK/V2 (ST debug probe)
modules.summary: Classic in-circuit debugger and programmer for STM32 and STM8 over SWD/JTAG/SWIM.
not_for: running application code (it is a debug probe, not a target)

modules.name: X-NUCLEO-IKS01A3 (X-NUCLEO expansion shield)

modules.summary: MEMS sensor-hub expansion board (LSM6DSV16X IMU with embedded sensor hub + Qvar, LIS2MDL, LIS2DUXS12, LPS22DF, SHT40AD) for Nucleo.

modules.name: X-NUCLEO-53L5A1 (X-NUCLEO expansion shield)
modules.summary: Time-of-Flight ranging expansion board carrying a VL53L5CX 8x8 multizone ToF sensor (plus spare breakout) for Nucleo.
not_for: standalone use (it is a shield, needs a Nucleo host)

modules.name: X-NUCLEO-BNRG2A1 (X-NUCLEO expansion shield)
modules.summary: Bluetooth Low Energy expansion board based on the BlueNRG-2 network processor, adding BLE 5.0 connectivity to any Nucleo.
good_for: adding BLE to a wired STM32 Nucleo
not_for: standalone use (it is a shield, needs a Nucleo host)

modules.name: X-NUCLEO-NFC08A1 (X-NUCLEO expansion shield)
modules.summary: Dynamic NFC/RFID tag expansion board based on the ST25DV64K, giving a Nucleo an energy-harvesting NFC Type-5 tag with I2C access.
not_for: standalone use (it is a shield, needs a Nucleo host)

modules.name: X-NUCLEO-IHM07M1 (X-NUCLEO expansion shield)
modules.summary: Three-phase brushless (BLDC/PMSM) motor driver expansion board based on the L6230 DMOS driver, for FOC/six-step motor control from a Nucleo.
not_for: standalone use (it is a shield, needs a Nucleo host)

modules.name: Hakko FX-888D soldering station
modules.summary: Digital 70 W temperature-controlled soldering station; the shop-standard workhorse for through-hole and most SMD hand work.
notes: Buy genuine Hakko T18 tips; clones run cold and oxidize fast.
The newer FX-888DX adds a cleaner UI but the FX-888D is the value pick.

modules.name: Pinecil V2 portable soldering iron
modules.summary: USB-C / DC pocket soldering iron (open IronOS firmware) that heats in seconds; the best cheap iron and a great travel/field tool.
good_for: powering from a USB-C PD pack or laptop charger
not_for: high-thermal-mass joints without a 60 W+ PD supply
a bench station replacement for all-day production
notes: Needs a 65 W USB-C PD or 12-20 V DC source to hit full power; a weak charger throttles it.
Uses Pine64/TS-100-style tips (JBC-C210-ish form factor).

modules.name: Weller WE1010 soldering station
modules.summary: 70 W digital station; the common Hakko FX-888D alternative with the classic Weller tip ecosystem.
good_for: general through-hole and SMD hand soldering
shops already standardized on Weller ET tips
notes: Uses Weller ET-series tips; plentiful but pricier than Hakko T18.

modules.name: JBC CD-2BE soldering station
modules.summary: Pro-grade station whose cartridge tips recover temperature almost instantly; the gold standard for production and rework benches.
good_for: lead-free work on heavy ground planes
not_for: hobby budgets (several times the price of an FX-888D)
notes: C210/C245 cartridge tips integrate the heater + sensor in the tip, which is why recovery is so fast.
Overkill for occasional hobby use; buy it when soldering is your job.

modules.name: Quick 861DW hot-air rework station
modules.summary: 1000 W brushless-fan hot-air station; the hobbyist favorite for SMD rework, chip removal, and reflowing fine-pitch parts.
good_for: removing/placing QFN, QFP, SOIC and small BGA
not_for: large BGA where a hotplate preheat is needed
notes: Preheat the board (hotplate/IR) before lifting large or ground-heavy parts to avoid cracking.
Brushless fan is quiet and long-lived vs cheaper diaphragm-pump guns.

modules.name: Hakko FR-301 desoldering gun
modules.summary: Self-contained vacuum desoldering gun that clears through-hole joints in one pass; a huge time-saver over wick + pump.
notes: Clean the filter chamber and nozzle regularly or suction dies.
The built-in pump beats the classic bulb/spring 'solder sucker' for repeated work.

modules.name: Miniware MHP30 mini hotplate
modules.summary: Palm-sized 30x30 mm reflow hotplate for small PCBs; preheats boards and reflows tiny solder-paste assemblies without an oven.
good_for: reflowing small boards and modules with solder paste
not_for: boards larger than ~45 mm (edges run cold)
notes: For larger or more repeatable reflow, a toaster oven with a Controleo3 controller and a real profile is the classic DIY upgrade.
Needs a 65 W USB-C PD supply to reach lead-free paste temps.

modules.name: Fluke 87V industrial multimeter
modules.summary: True-RMS industrial handheld DMM; the reference-grade meter for accuracy, safety rating, and decades of reliability.
good_for: CAT III/IV mains and industrial work
not_for: bench logging/data capture (no PC link on base model)
notes: CAT III 1000 V / CAT IV 600 V safety rating matters when probing mains.
If you only do low-voltage electronics, the cheaper Fluke 117 or a Brymen covers it.

modules.name: Fluke 117 electrician's multimeter
modules.summary: True-RMS handheld DMM with non-contact voltage detect; Fluke reliability at a more accessible price than the 87V.

modules.name: Brymen BM235 multimeter
modules.summary: True-RMS handheld (the EEVblog-badged favorite) offering near-Fluke build and features for roughly half the price.
good_for: temperature, capacitance, duty cycle, low-Z mode
not_for: those who need the Fluke service/calibration ecosystem
notes: Sold in some regions as the EEVblog BM235; same meter.

modules.name: Aneng AN8008 pocket multimeter
modules.summary: Cheap true-RMS pocket DMM; a fine throw-in-the-bag second meter or a no-risk first meter for low-voltage electronics.
good_for: low-voltage bench electronics on a tight budget
not_for: mains or high-energy circuits (don't trust the CAT rating)
notes: Treat the safety rating as marketing; keep it on low-voltage DC/logic work, not mains.

modules.name: Rigol DM3058E bench multimeter
modules.summary: 5.5-digit bench DMM with USB/LAN; adds resolution, stability, and PC logging a handheld can't match.
not_for: fast transient capture (that's a scope's job)

modules.name: Rigol DHO804 oscilloscope
modules.summary: 12-bit 70 MHz 4-channel desktop scope; a compact, high-resolution entry scope that punches far above its price.
good_for: embedded / power / analog debug up to ~70 MHz
not_for: high-bandwidth RF or fast digital edges (>70 MHz)
notes: The 4-channel model is worth it if you ever debug SPI + I2C (or clock + data + CS) together.
Bandwidth can often be upgraded by license; buy the bandwidth you need now.

modules.name: Rigol DHO914S oscilloscope
modules.summary: 12-bit 125 MHz 4-channel scope with a built-in 25 MHz function generator and logic-analyzer option; a near-complete bench in one box.
good_for: mixed-signal debug with the built-in AWG and optional logic pod
12-bit resolution at higher bandwidth than the DHO804
not_for: deep protocol work needing many logic channels

modules.name: Siglent SDS1104X-E oscilloscope
modules.summary: Classic 100 MHz 4-channel 8-bit scope with deep protocol decode and fast waveform update; the long-standing value benchmark.
not_for: low-level signals where 12-bit scopes (DHO series) resolve more
notes: Great used/new value; the newer 12-bit Rigol DHO series is the main alternative to weigh.

modules.name: Rigol DS1054Z oscilloscope
modules.summary: The classic budget 50 MHz 4-channel scope that launched a generation of hobby benches; still a solid cheap first scope.
notes: Largely superseded by the 12-bit DHO800/900 at similar money; buy used or if you want the proven classic.

modules.name: Keysight DSOX1204G oscilloscope
modules.summary: Pro-tier 70-200 MHz 4-channel scope with a built-in WaveGen AWG; Keysight's low-noise front end and software in an entry chassis.
good_for: professional labs wanting Keysight quality on a budget chassis
not_for: hobby budgets (costs well above the Rigol/Siglent class)

modules.name: Saleae Logic 8 logic analyzer
modules.summary: 8-channel USB logic + analog analyzer with best-in-class software; the pro standard for protocol capture and decode.
good_for: mixed digital+analog capture on one tool
not_for: tight budgets (the software, not hardware, is what you pay for)
notes: The Saleae software works with cheaper hardware for casual use; you pay Saleae for the polish and support.

modules.name: DSLogic Plus logic analyzer
modules.summary: 16-channel USB analyzer with deep sample buffer and the open DSView software; a strong mid-tier alternative to Saleae.
good_for: longer/faster captures than cheap FX2 clones
not_for: those who specifically need Saleae's decoder library

modules.name: Generic FX2 8-channel logic analyzer
modules.summary: The ubiquitous ~$10 USB logic analyzer based on the Cypress FX2LP; works great with free sigrok/PulseView for slow buses.
good_for: cheap first logic analyzer for I2C/UART/slow SPI
a throwaway tool you won't cry over
not_for: fast buses (reliable only to a few MHz over USB)
notes: Flash it / use it with sigrok; the bundled vendor software is poor.
Sampling above ~8-24 MHz drops samples on USB 2.0; keep it to slow signals.

modules.name: Korad KA3005P bench power supply
modules.summary: Single-channel 30 V / 5 A linear programmable PSU with USB control; the standard affordable first bench supply.
good_for: clean low-noise power for analog/RF prototyping
current-limit (CC) protection while bringing up new boards
notes: Set the current limit before powering a new board; CC mode saves smoke on shorts.
Linear regulation = low noise, but it runs warm and heavy vs switching supplies.

modules.name: Rigol DP832 triple-output power supply
modules.summary: 3-channel programmable PSU (30 V/3 A, 30 V/3 A, 5 V/3 A) with readback and logging; the go-to multi-rail bench supply.
good_for: powering boards that need +rail, -rail, and logic together
not_for: tight budgets (step up from a single Korad)
notes: The low (5 V/3 A) channel is perfect for logic while the two 30 V rails feed op-amps/analog.

modules.name: Siglent SPD3303X power supply
modules.summary: Triple-output programmable PSU (2x 32 V/3.2 A + fixed rail) with a bright display and series/parallel modes; a strong DP832 rival.
good_for: dual-tracking rails for op-amp / analog bring-up
series/parallel for higher V or A

modules.name: Siglent SDG1032X function/arbitrary generator
modules.summary: 2-channel 30 MHz arbitrary waveform generator; injects clean test signals, sweeps, and arbitrary waveforms for analog/filter/sensor work.
good_for: stimulating filters, amplifiers, and sensor front ends
two independent channels for differential or clock+data
not_for: simple cases already covered by a scope's built-in AWG
notes: If your scope already has a built-in generator (e.g. DHO914S), you may not need a standalone AWG yet.

modules.name: SEGGER J-Link BASE / EDU debug probe
modules.summary: The industry-standard JTAG/SWD debug probe with fast flash download and broad toolchain support; EDU variant is a cheap non-commercial option.
good_for: fast, reliable flashing in CI and at the bench
not_for: commercial use on the low-cost EDU licence (licensing restriction)
non-ARM targets outside its supported list
notes: J-Link EDU / EDU Mini are for students and hobbyists only; buy BASE/PLUS for commercial work.
RTT gives you printf-style logging over SWD with no extra UART.

modules.name: ST-LINK/V3 debug probe (STLINK-V3SET)
modules.summary: ST's JTAG/SWD programmer-debugger for STM32/STM8 with a virtual COM port and bridge functions; cheap and essential for ST work.
not_for: features of a full J-Link on exotic cores
notes: The ST-LINK on a Nucleo/Discovery board can be used standalone; ST-LINK also appears as a dev board in the ST set.
STLINK-V3MINIE is a tiny low-cost variant for embedding in a jig.

modules.name: Black Magic Probe
modules.summary: Open-source SWD/JTAG probe with an on-board GDB server - no OpenOCD needed; just connect GDB straight to the probe.
good_for: GDB-native ARM Cortex-M debugging with zero middleware
a built-in USB UART alongside debug
not_for: targets outside its supported ARM set
notes: Presents two USB serial ports: one is the GDB server, one is a passthrough UART.

modules.name: DAPLink / CMSIS-DAP probe
modules.summary: Open CMSIS-DAP debug probe standard found on many dev boards and cheap standalone adapters; drag-and-drop flashing plus SWD debug.
good_for: cheap, open, cross-vendor ARM SWD debugging
works with pyOCD / OpenOCD out of the box
notes: CMSIS-DAP is the protocol; DAPLink is Arm's reference firmware - many boards expose it already.

modules.name: Nordic Power Profiler Kit II (PPK2)
modules.summary: Source-meter + ampere-meter that measures nA-to-amp current draw over time; the essential tool for optimizing battery-powered firmware.
good_for: profiling sleep/active current of low-power MCUs and sensors
finding the firmware event that spikes consumption
not_for: lab-grade DC analysis (Otii is more capable)
notes: Can both power the DUT (source mode) and measure an externally powered one (ampere mode).
Dynamic range covers ~200 nA to 1 A - ideal for coin-cell / energy-harvesting work.

modules.name: Qoitech Otii Arc Pro power analyzer
modules.summary: Pro power source/analyzer combining a precise programmable supply, high-res current logging, and UART capture in one tool.
good_for: correlating current with device UART logs on one timeline
repeatable supply + measurement for test benches

modules.name: AmScope SE400-Z stereo microscope
modules.summary: Binocular stereo zoom microscope with long working distance; the real tool for SMD inspection, fine soldering, and rework under magnification.
good_for: inspecting joints and PCB damage in true stereo/3D
long working distance to fit an iron underneath
not_for: screen-sharing / recording (no camera; add a trinocular model for that)
notes: Stereo (two eyepieces) gives the depth perception a flat USB scope can't; worth it for rework.
A boom/articulating stand beats a pillar stand for working over a board.

modules.name: Generic USB / HDMI digital microscope
modules.summary: Cheap digital microscope on a stand that shows a magnified PCB on a screen; fine for inspection and light SMD work on a budget.
good_for: budget SMD inspection and basic rework
showing/recording a board on a monitor
not_for: true stereo depth (it's a flat 2D image)
notes: Prefer an HDMI model with its own screen over a USB-to-PC one for less latency while soldering.
Short working distance on many units leaves no room for an iron; check before buying.

modules.name: RTL-SDR Blog V4 dongle
modules.summary: The best-regarded RTL2832U receive-only SDR dongle (~500 kHz-1.75 GHz) with a TCXO, bias-tee, and improved front end; the standard cheap SDR.
good_for: learning SDR, ADS-B, AIS, pagers, weather-sat, general RX
stable tuning (1 PPM TCXO) vs generic dongles
HF reception via its built-in direct-sampling
notes: A distinct, higher-quality product than the generic RTL2832U dongle already in the catalog; insist on the genuine 'RTL-SDR Blog V4' to get the TCXO and filtering.
Needs the RTL-SDR Blog driver branch for the V4's R828D front end.

modules.name: Airspy Mini SDR
modules.summary: Receive-only SDR with a 12-bit ADC and up to 6 MSPS; a big step up in dynamic range and bandwidth from an RTL-SDR dongle.
good_for: cleaner RX with 12-bit dynamic range (24-1800 MHz)
serious VHF/UHF monitoring and spectrum work
not_for: the lowest budgets (costs more than an RTL dongle)

modules.name: Hakko CHP-170 flush cutters
modules.summary: Precise micro flush cutters for trimming component leads clean to the board; a cheap tool you'll reach for constantly.
good_for: flush-trimming through-hole leads and zip ties
not_for: hardened steel wire or music wire (will nick the jaws)
notes: Keep a dedicated pair for soft metals only; cutting steel ruins the flush edge.

modules.name: Engineer PA-09 crimping pliers
modules.summary: Japanese universal crimper that does open-barrel contacts (Dupont, JST, Molex, JAM) extremely well; the hobbyist's connector-crimping answer.
good_for: one tool across many connector families
neat, reliable crimps without a per-series die set
notes: The PA-09 handles the common 2.0/2.54 mm hobby connectors; PA-21 covers larger barrels.

modules.name: Anti-static precision tweezers set
modules.summary: A set of fine ESD-safe tweezers (straight, curved, fine-point) for placing SMD parts and handling small components.
good_for: handling leads and wires under a microscope
not_for: prying or heavy mechanical work (fine tips bend)
notes: Get at least one straight and one curved (bent-tip) pair; the curved pair is what you'll use most for SMD.

modules.name: Stickvise PCB vise
modules.summary: Low-profile spring-loaded PCB vise that holds a board flat at bench level; ideal for soldering, probing, and inspection.
good_for: holding a bare PCB steady while soldering or probing
low, stable profile that fits under a microscope
not_for: holding odd-shaped or very large assemblies
work needing many articulated arms (use a third-hand)

modules.name: PanaVise 201 Junior PCB holder
modules.summary: Articulating multi-position vise head that tilts and rotates to any angle; the classic 'position the board where you want it' holder.
good_for: tilting/rotating a board to any working angle
holding assemblies, not just bare PCBs
pairing with the PanaVise base + accessories system
not_for: very low-profile microscope work (Stickvise sits flatter)

modules.name: Third-hand / helping-hands tool
modules.summary: Flexible gooseneck or alligator-clip arms that hold wires and boards together for soldering; the cheapest way to get extra hands.
good_for: holding two wires together to tin/solder
models with magnifier and base clips
not_for: rigid, precise PCB holding (use a Stickvise/PanaVise)
notes: Gooseneck/magnetic-base versions hold position far better than the classic two-alligator-clip cast base.

modules.name: Kester 63/37 leaded solder (0.031 in)
modules.summary: Eutectic 63/37 tin-lead rosin-core solder - the easiest-flowing, most forgiving solder for hand work and the default for learning.
good_for: beginner-friendly hand soldering (sharp eutectic melt point)
not_for: food/consumer contact or where lead is prohibited
notes: Lead is toxic: wash hands, don't eat at the bench, and use fume extraction.
0.031 in (0.8 mm) is the versatile default gauge; go thinner (0.02 in) for fine SMD.

modules.name: SAC305 lead-free solder wire
modules.summary: Rosin-core SAC305 (Sn96.5/Ag3/Cu0.5) lead-free solder for RoHS-compliant work; needs more heat and good flux to wet well.
not_for: beginners learning to solder (less forgiving than 63/37)
notes: Run ~20-30 C hotter than leaded and keep extra flux handy; joints look duller than leaded - that's normal.

modules.name: Soldering flux (no-clean paste / pen)
modules.summary: Extra flux (gel in a syringe or a flux pen) that makes solder wet and flow; essential for SMD, rework, and drag-soldering.
not_for: leaving on uncleaned for high-impedance analog (clean residues there)
replacing cored-solder flux for simple through-hole
notes: No-clean residue is usually fine to leave, but clean it off high-impedance / RF nodes with IPA.
Amtech-style tacky gel flux in a syringe is the hobby favorite for QFN/BGA work.

modules.name: Solder wick / desoldering braid
modules.summary: Flux-impregnated copper braid that wicks molten solder off pads and joints; the simplest desoldering and cleanup consumable.
good_for: cleaning excess solder off pads and bridges
not_for: clearing deep plated-through holes in bulk (a desolder gun is faster)
heat-sensitive pads (braid pulls a lot of heat)
notes: Match braid width to the job; add a little flux and let the braid - not the pad - take the heat.
No.2 / ~2 mm width is the handy all-rounder.

modules.name: Kapton (polyimide) tape
modules.summary: High-temperature polyimide tape that masks areas during hot-air rework and reflow; also handy for temporary insulation.
good_for: masking adjacent parts during hot-air rework

modules.name: Isopropyl alcohol >=99% (flux cleaner)
modules.summary: High-purity (>=99%) isopropyl alcohol for removing flux residue and cleaning boards; the standard bench solvent.
good_for: cleaning flux residue off finished boards
not_for: use near open flame / hot iron (flammable)
cleaning sensitive membrane switches or some plastics
notes: Use >=99% (anhydrous); drugstore 70% leaves water behind and dries slowly.
An acid brush or no-lint swab plus IPA lifts no-clean residue off RF/high-impedance nodes.

modules.name: ESD wrist strap + mat grounding kit
modules.summary: Grounded anti-static wrist strap and dissipative bench mat; cheap insurance against zapping MOSFETs, MCUs, and RF front ends.
good_for: handling static-sensitive ICs, MOSFETs, and RF parts
basic ESD discipline at any bench
not_for: live-mains work (never wear a hard-grounded strap near mains)
replacing proper ESD flooring/footwear in a controlled facility
notes: Clip the mat and strap to a common ground point (a known-good mains earth), not directly to a hot chassis.
A 1 Mohm resistor is built into the strap lead for safety - don't bypass it.
